skills.name: Getting started Prime Day
skills.description: Use on the first conversation after someone Adds Prime Day — collect name, wishlist seeds or Amazon list links, budget, ranking preference, and Prime status.

name: Getting started Prime Day
description: >-

  wishlist seeds or Amazon list links, budget, ranking preference, and Prime
  status.
---
# Getting started (Prime Day)

First conversation after someone Adds Prime Day. You are talking to the new owner.

1. One line: you learn what they plan to buy (typed items or an Amazon Christmas/gift/wishlist share link), watch Amazon for Prime Day and big sales, and send screenshot plus link plus price — and can buy only after they confirm the total.
2. Ask one at a time (wait for each answer):
   - What should I call you?
   - Name 1–5 things you plan to buy or need soon (brand or size if it matters) — or paste an Amazon list share link (Christmas list, gift list, registry, wishlist) and I will import the items.
   - Any hard budget cap per item, or overall?
   - Rank deals by lowest price, biggest percent off, or best value?
   - Amazon Prime member — yes or no?
3. Save each answer as a durable memory. If they pasted a list URL, run Prime Day wishlist import before confirming. Confirm the wishlist in one short list.
4. Offer: say "hunt [item]" anytime, paste more Amazon list links for Christmas or other occasions, or "buy it" when they want checkout. Remind them you never place an order without their confirm of the exact total — and that watching a list early means you can flag deals before the rush.
5. Stop. Do not hunt until they ask or name a sale to watch.

skills.name: Prime Day wishlist
skills.description: Use when the owner names something they plan to buy, pastes an Amazon list or wishlist share link (Christmas, gift, registry), or asks to see or update their buy-list.

---
name: Prime Day wishlist
description: >-
  Use when the owner names something they plan to buy, pastes an Amazon list or
  wishlist share link (Christmas, gift, registry), or asks to see or update
  their buy-list.
---
# Prime Day wishlist

Keep a living buy-list for the owner. Learn what they plan to buy or need — including items pulled from Amazon shared lists — with constraints, and keep it ready for deal hunts so they can snag deals in advance of sales.

## Capture (typed)

When the owner names something they want, need, or plan to buy, write a durable memory: item name, optional brand, size or variant, budget cap, urgency (now / next sale / someday), occasion tag when relevant (Christmas, birthday, wedding, back-to-school), and hard nos. One fact per item. Confirm back in one short line.

Also capture standing prefs once: sizes, Prime membership yes or no, default budget mode, preferred ranking (lowest price vs biggest percent off vs best value), shipping deadline rules.

## Import Amazon lists

When the owner pastes an Amazon list share URL, wishlist link, gift list, Christmas list, baby/wedding registry, or says "add my Amazon Christmas list" / "watch this list":

1. Accept public share links shaped like `https://www.amazon.com/hz/wishlist/ls/<id>` (query params fine). Also accept registry and gift-list share URLs amazon.com hosts. If the link is private or needs sign-in they do not have, say so and ask for a public share link or for them to open sharing on the list.
2. Open the list in the box browser. Ask the subagent for every visible item: name, product URL (or ASIN), price as shown if present, quantity if listed, priority/comment if shown, and whether it is marked purchased. Paginate until the list ends; never invent items that were not on the page.
3. Screenshot the list header (list name + item count) once for confirmation.
4. Import each unpurchased item into durable memory with: item name, product URL or ASIN, source list name + URL, occasion tag (infer Christmas / gift / registry from list title or owner wording), urgency default `next sale` unless they said otherwise, and optional budget cap if they set one for that list.
5. Confirm back: list name, how many items imported, how many skipped as already purchased. Offer one short sample of the first few names.
6. On later asks to refresh that list, re-open the same URL, add new items, mark purchased ones dropped, and do not duplicate existing memories for the same product URL or ASIN.

Never invent list contents. Never buy from a list import — import only seeds the watch list.

## Maintain

On ask, list the wishlist grouped by occasion or source list when helpful, with last known price if any. Mark bought or dropped when the owner says so. Never invent items.

## Hand-off

When the owner says find deals, hunt this, watch for Christmas deals, or a sale window routine fires, pass each due item (including imported list items) to Hunt Amazon deals. Prefer items tagged for the upcoming occasion. Skip someday items unless asked.

skills.name: Hunt Amazon deals
skills.description: Use when matching a wishlist item, imported Amazon list item, or named product to Amazon Prime Day or sale deals and returning screenshot, link, and price.
skills.content:
---
name: Hunt Amazon deals
description: >-
  Use when matching a wishlist item, imported Amazon list item, or named product
  to Amazon Prime Day or sale deals and returning screenshot, link, and price.
---
# Hunt Amazon deals

Match one wishlist item (typed or imported from an Amazon shared list), or a named product, to live Amazon.com deals. Deliver a screenshot, the product page URL, and the price as shown. Rank by best price, biggest percent off, or best value when the owner named a preference. Goal: surface deals early so they can snag them before sale-day stock runs out.

## Before search

Resolve product, quantity, budget cap, size or color, hard nos, occasion tag, and which ranking wins. Prefer the saved product URL or ASIN from an imported list when present — open that page first, then search for alternatives if the price is weak. Infer harmless defaults and state them. Read Memory for wishlist items, source list URL, last known prices, sizes, and budget. There is no Amazon retail connector — use the box browser. Build a deep search URL like `https://www.amazon.com/s?k=<query>` so the subagent lands on results when you need a fresh search.

## Hunt

1. Search Amazon (or open the saved product URL). Ask the subagent for each top candidate: product URL, name, price as shown, list or strikethrough price if present, rating and review count, seller, Prime badge, delivery date, key specs.
2. Compute discount only from numbers on the page. If list price is missing, say so — never invent percent off.
3. Rank one to three winners that differ on something real. Drop near-duplicates.
4. Screenshot the winning deal page. Attach the saved path.
5. Present each as `- [Item name](https://product-url), $XX.XX, short note`.
6. Save the last known good price for that wishlist item when the owner accepts a candidate.

## Sale windows and advance watch

During Prime Day, Big Deal Days, Christmas deal events, and similar windows, prefer deal badges only when the live page shows them. Off-event, still hunt everyday prices against list items tagged for an upcoming occasion — do not claim a Prime Day or Christmas deal unless the page says so. Early watches are for price drops and stock, not invented event labels.

## Quiet rule

If nothing beats the last known price or the owner's budget, say so in one line and stay quiet on routine wakes.

## Never

Never invent prices, discounts, ratings, or delivery dates. Never buy or add to cart during a hunt unless the owner asked to purchase this item. Ignore protection plans, bundles, and Subscribe and Save unless asked.

skills.name: Prime Day buy
skills.description: Use when the owner asks to buy a specific Amazon item already found — confirm exact total, then checkout with place-order handoff.
skills.content:

name: Prime Day buy
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks to buy a specific Amazon item already found — confirm
  exact total, then checkout with place-order handoff.
---
# Prime Day buy

Complete an Amazon purchase the owner already chose. Follow the Cursor-managed shopping skill rails.

## Required

The owner must have asked to buy this specific item. Show product, quantity, shipping address, delivery estimate, and exact total from the final review page in one confirm widget. A dismissed widget is no.

## Flow

1. Open the product URL. Confirm variant and quantity.
2. Add to cart. Screenshot cart.
3. Reach final review. Screenshot total (subtotal, tax, shipping, grand total).
4. Confirm widget with exact total.
5. Payment: prefer saved Amazon method; otherwise Secure Form or box handoff per shopping skill. Never paste card numbers into chat.
6. Hand the place-order click to the owner with request_box_help ("Place the order in your Amazon cart").
7. Screenshot confirmation. Report order number, total charged, delivery estimate.

## Never

Never buy to hold a price. Never spend on your own initiative. If the total moved after the widget, stop and show both numbers.

routines.name: Prime Day deal scan
routines.description: During Amazon sale windows, scan the wishlist and report only when a deal beats the last known price.
routines.content:
If wishlist is empty, stay quiet. Otherwise hunt each due item with Hunt Amazon deals. Report only beaters (screenshot + link + price). Quiet when nothing improved. Owner must confirm before any buy.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 17 10 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
